The fund seeks to track the Markit iBoxx USD Liquid High Yield Index and invest in U.S. dollar-denominated high yield corporate bonds.
The fund is classified as Fixed Income and is described as exposure to non-investment grade corporate credit.
The fund launch date is 04/04/2007, distribution frequency is monthly, the exchange is NYSE Arca, and the CUSIP is 464288513.
Net assets are listed as $16,378.81M and shares outstanding as 206,400,000.
The fund expense ratio and management fee are both shown as 0.49%; Acquired Fund Fees and Expenses and Other Expenses are shown as 0.00%.
The document shows a 30 Day SEC Yield of 6.70%.
Calendar year performance is shown for 2021 through 2025, with NAV returns of 4.12, -11.37, 12.41, 7.70, and 8.56, and market price returns of 3.75, -10.99, 11.53, 7.97, and 8.60.
Annualized performance is shown for NAV, market price, and benchmark across since inception, 1-year, 3-year, 5-year, and 10-year periods.
The annualized performance table shows benchmark returns of 7.13 since inception, 8.41 for 1-year, 4.11 for 3-year, 5.62 for 5-year, and 5.46 for 10-year.
Portfolio metrics shown include Equity Beta (3y) 0.30, Weighted Avg Maturity 3.82 years, Effective Duration 3.02 years, Standard Deviation (3y) 4.57%, Convexity -0.15, and Number of Holdings 1,321.

Visible top holdings include BLK CSH FND TREASURY SL AGENCY Fund, 1261229 BC LTD 144A, QUIKRETE HOLDINGS INC 144A, SV RNO PROPERTY OWNER 1 LLC 144A, ASURION LLC 144A, CLOUD SOFTWARE GROUP INC 144A, ECHOSTAR CORP, DISH NETWORK CORP 144A, and WULF COMPUTE LLC 144A.

The document shows sector and credit-quality breakdowns, including BB Rated 56.87%, B Rated 29.96%, and CCC Rated 10.47%.
The document states that holdings and allocations are subject to change.
The document states that ratings come from S&P, Moody’s, and Fitch, are mapped to S&P major rating categories, and use the median rating when all three agencies are available.
The document defines below-investment-grade as BB and below, and says unrated securities do not necessarily indicate low quality.
The document explains that ETF shares trade at market price, not NAV, and are not individually redeemed from the fund.
The document says brokerage commissions, if applicable, will reduce returns.

review.summary: The factsheet provides solid basic coverage of the ETF’s identity, benchmark, fee level, yield metric, portfolio characteristics, holdings, and historical performance. It also discloses key high-yield, interest-rate, credit, and ETF trading risks, plus standard past-performance limitations. The main limitations are incomplete or truncated disclosure text in places and the absence of a fully consolidated explanation linking fees, tracking, and performance.
learning_next_steps: Review how expense ratio, SEC yield, and market-price returns are different concepts in ETF factsheets.
Compare the document’s risk disclosures with its portfolio credit-quality and maturity breakdowns to understand why high-yield bond funds carry specific risks.
Look for benchmark methodology and tracking-related disclosures in a full prospectus if you want to study how funds describe index tracking.
